crime_highlights: the appellant produced a handgun and was gesturing with it
The appellant shot one of the occupants of the house in the leg, causing a non-life-threatening injury
At the time of the offence, the appellant was prohibited from possessing a firearm

crime_highlights: The child pornography count involved the appellant discussing with others online that he was committing sexual crimes against his own children and his partner’s child
he would book a hotel room to take his children to so another person could have a sexual encounter with them
The crimes are undoubtedly very serious
rationale_highlights: the appellant has wholly embraced his Indigenous identity, culture and traditions while in prison
the clear progress that the appellant has made in relation to connecting with his culture
we are prepared to reduce the sentence by six months
note: No Gladue report; reduction tied to cultural reconnection and mitigating factors.

crime_highlights: He tackled her from behind as she walked toward her refrigerator
R.S. responded by grabbing her throat and squeezing hard
The victim went to her bed, cried, and lay in a fetal position
The sexual assault left the victim with a red mark and bruising on her neck and stomach
rationale_highlights: this was a case in which R.S.’s moral culpability could rightly be considered to be reduced by his background
family violence, alcohol abuse, and family breakups are sequelae of colonialism and intergenerational trauma
I have little doubt that this part of your early life played a part in this offence
The reality is that your unique personal circumstances, viewed contextually, diminishes your moral culpability
note: Paras 60-62 are Paciocco J.A. concurring, describing trial judge findings; para 40 majority.
